ratings_why.fun: Deaths becoming Compost that ripens into Fruits is satisfying to watch grow, but Fruits spend on their own, so the hoard half fights the spend half.
ratings_why.distinct: Paying Fruits in reading order, like making change, is fresh; the rest is a familiar deaths-matter and third-counter pattern.

verdict_why: Warden Amanita, Bootlace with Puffwell, and Old Fingers each have wording that doesn't say what happens; those are quick fixes worth one more pass.

points.text: Warden Amanita's "share its stats" can be read two ways: split between the neighbours, or each gets the full stats. Say which.
Grandmother Bootlace with Bellows Puffwell's "repeated while you can pay" is unclear: does each paid fire get a free twin, or is just the first one doubled? Spell it out on one of the two cards.
Old Fingers doesn't say what happens with no unit next to it. Do you still gain 4 Compost? Add "if you can" or say it always pays.
Fruits fire whether you want them to or not, so a hoarder must leave them off the board. Letting a Fruit be skipped ("you may spend") would join builds A and D instead of keeping them apart.
Foxfire Lantern-bearer and Guildmaster Ashcake read as the same card at two sizes. Giving the Lantern a lantern-like twist, such as lighting only the touching run, would make it worth reading.

standouts.why: Clerk Inkcap writes in his own ink and shrinks a Health each time it pays: the card plays its lore exactly, and you can read it at a glance.
Hired Mute turns the sell button into a silent burial for Compost: one plain line, and a real decision every turn.
Stinkhorn, Herald hits whoever is across when a friend falls. It's easy to read on the board and it makes where you place units matter.

weakest.why: Foxfire Lantern-bearer is a smaller copy of Ashcake's hoard read, with little of its own.
Dewdrop Bonnet is pure counter maths with no woodland picture in what it does.
Grandmother Bootlace's text is generic "triggers twice" rules; the patient, everywhere-at-once founder doesn't come through.

flags.note: "Share its stats": split or copied in full?
How the free second trigger works with Puffwell's repeat isn't written.
The text doesn't say what happens with no unit next to it.
Puffwell with Three-Rain Mourner and Bootlace gives the whole board +8/+8 or so a turn; worth the owner's eye.
